descriptions.text: The ABCCApp contract issued DDDD reward tokens based on user-controlled deposit and configuration state without restricting who could set the reward parameters or how rewards scaled relative to the deposited stake. Using a BUSD flash loan, the attacker deposited into ABCCApp, then called the unprotected addFixedDay(1_000_000_000) to inflate the reward accrual basis, and finally claimDDDD() to mint/claim a disproportionate amount of DDDD tokens. The harvested DDDD was swapped through a PancakeSwap V3 multi-hop path (DDDD -> WBNB -> BSC-USD) back into BUSD, the flash loan was repaid, and the attacker kept the spread (~10,062 BUSD). Vulnerable code snippet: Attack Tx: https://bscscan.com/tx/0xee4eae6f70a6894c09fda645fb24ab841e9847a788b1b2e8cb9cc50c1866fb12 Analysis: https://x.com/TenArmorAlert/status/1959457212914352530

ABCCApp on BSC was reportedly attacked, resulting in a loss of approximately $10.1K. The root cause was that the contract’s addFixedDay() function lacked access control, and fixedDay was used in calculating claimable USDT.
